location.scope: Bali-wide; verify local and site-specific rules

content.definition: Visitors should dress appropriately for the setting and avoid photography or public behavior that disrespects people, ceremonies, sacred places, or religious symbols.
content.cultural_context: The 2025 Governor Circular asks foreign tourists to dress modestly and respectfully in sacred areas, attractions, public places, and activities in Bali. It prohibits indecent or inappropriate photographs, including nudity, when these desecrate sacred places, temples, sacred objects, or religious symbols.
content.significance: Clothing and photography can affect dignity, privacy, and the sanctity of a place or event.
common_situations: Taking photos of residents or performers
Visiting public attractions or sacred sites

do: Dress respectfully and follow venue-specific clothing requirements
Ask permission before close-up portraits of identifiable people
Follow photography signs and organizer instructions
dont: Take or publish indecent or nude photographs at sacred places
Assume public access means unrestricted photography

common_misconceptions: The circular's dress guidance does not mean every venue has the same dress code.
Photography rules may vary by location and event.
regional_variations: Temples, ceremonies, private businesses, and public events may each have their own requirements.
content.additional_notes: Consent for portraits is a courtesy recommendation; the circular specifically addresses respectful dress and indecent photography at sacred places.

sources.title: Bali Governor Circular Letter No. 07 of 2025 on Foreign Tourist Conduct
Official Do and Don't Card for Foreign Tourists while in Bali

verification.verification_notes: Dress and sacred-site restrictions are source-supported. General consent guidance should be validated with local tourism/community stakeholders.

sensitivity.handling_notes: Use neutral, precise wording; distinguish formal rules from courtesy recommendations.
